title: Exactness of maps with the prescribed derived-couple equations
statement:
Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], and let $s\in\mathbf N$.
Let $D^{p,q},E^{p,q}$ be objects for $p,q\in\mathbf Z$, with maps
$a:D^{p,q}\to D^{p-1,q+1}$, $f:E^{p,q}\to D^{p+2,q-1}$,
and $g:D^{p,q}\to E^{p+s,q-s}$. Put $d^{p,q}=g^{p+2,q-1}f^{p,q}$.
Let $\beta^{p,q}:E^{p-s-2,q+s+1}\to E^{p,q}$ be the incoming $d$, with the
canonical transport of its target indices, and assume $d^{p,q}\beta^{p,q}=0$
and $f^{p+s,q-s}g^{p,q}=0$. Put
$D'^{p,q}=\operatorname{im}(a^{p+1,q-1})$ and
$E'^{p,q}=\operatorname{coker}(\widehat\beta^{p,q})$, where
$\widehat\beta$ is the lift of $\beta$ to $K^{p,q}=\ker d^{p,q}$.
Write $I^{p,q}:D'^{p,q}\to D^{p,q}$ for the transported image inclusion,
$A^{p,q}:D^{p+1,q-1}\to D'^{p,q}$ for the image epimorphism,
$P^{p,q}:K^{p,q}\to E'^{p,q}$ for the cokernel projection,
and $\widehat g^{r,t}:D^{r,t}\to K^{r+s,t-s}$ for the kernel lift of $g$.
All transports are the unique equality morphisms from the displayed integer identities.
Assume also $a^{p+2,q-1}f^{p,q}=0$, $g^{p-1,q+1}a^{p,q}=0$,
and $\operatorname{im}f^{p,q}=\ker a^{p+2,q-1}$,
$\operatorname{im}g^{p,q}=\ker f^{p+s,q-s}$,
$\operatorname{im}a^{p,q}=\ker g^{p-1,q+1}$ at every bidegree.
Let $a':D'^{p,q}\to D'^{p-1,q+1}$ be the explicit restriction of $a$
from [lem-sp-derived-map-construction]. Suppose maps
$f':E'^{p,q}\to D'^{p+2,q-1}$ and
$g':D'^{p,q}\to E'^{p+s+1,q-s-1}$ satisfy the defining equations
$I^{p-1,q+1}a'^{p,q}=a^{p,q}I^{p,q}$,
$I^{p+2,q-1}f'^{p,q}P^{p,q}=f^{p,q}\iota_K^{p,q}$,
and
$g'^{p,q}A^{p,q}=P^{p+s+1,q-s-1}\widehat g^{p+1,q-1}$,
with canonical target transport in the last equation.
Then $\operatorname{im}f'^{p,q}=\ker a'^{p+2,q-1}$,
$\operatorname{im}g'^{p,q}=\ker f'^{p+s+1,q-s-1}$, and
$\operatorname{im}a'^{p,q}=\ker g'^{p-1,q+1}$ at every bidegree.
This assertion does not construct any maps.

source.place: Lemma 12.21.2, Tag 011R, setup (4)-(6) and conclusion (3); Remark 12.21.5, Tag 0AMJ and its footnote; https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/011R and https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/0AMJ

proof.text: Apply the generalized-element calculus with epimorphic refinements: kernel membership means annihilation, image membership means a lift after an epimorphism, and subobject membership descends along epimorphisms by the kernel-of-cokernel description of a mono.

At D′, an element killed by a′ is killed by the original a after the mono inclusion. Lift it through f using im f = ker a. This f-lift is a cycle since its f-image lies in im a = ker g. Its cycle quotient class is an f′-preimage by the defining equation. Conversely f′-images are killed by a′, by the original f-then-a zero relation and epi/mono cancellation.

At E′, lift a class killed by f′ to cycles along the cokernel projection after epimorphic refinement. Its f-image is zero by the f′ equation and mono cancellation. Lift through g using im g = ker f, and apply the incoming image epimorphism of a to this lift. The g′ equation shows this image is a preimage of the class. Conversely g′-images are killed by f′ by the original g-then-f relation and the defining equations.

At the next D′, lift an element killed by g′ along the image epimorphism of a. Its g-image is a boundary by the g′ equation and the kernel description of the cycle projection. Lift that boundary through the incoming differential, after refinement, and subtract the corresponding f-image from the chosen lift. Its a-image is unchanged since f followed by a is zero, and its g-image is now zero. Lift it through a using ker g = im a. The a′ equation gives the needed a′-preimage. The converse follows by the same equations from a followed by g being zero. Descend all memberships along the chosen epimorphisms to obtain equalities of subobjects.
